summary: Tested (1) OraChatHouseRulesPanel Chat/Video switcher and (2) fal.ai BYOK key + Universal Key fallback (3 backend endpoints + Admin Settings card). Backend 5/5 PASS. Frontend fal.ai BYOK end-to-end PASS with 1 cosmetic double-ellipsis defect. House Rules switcher has 2 real UX bugs: (a) per-scope textarea state is LOST when the user switches tabs (state should persist per spec), (b) initialScope prop is not honoured when the panel opens from a drawer already in Video mode — panel still opens on Chat tab.

ui_bugs.issue: Video-tab textarea state is not preserved when switching Chat -> Video -> back to Video. Filled 'TEST_INDEPENDENT_VIDEO_XYZ' in Video textarea, switched to Chat, switched back to Video: text resets to server-loaded value and Save button becomes disabled again (dirty=false). Root cause: parent renders `scope === 'chat' ? <ChatRulesBody /> : <VideoRulesBody />` so the inactive body unmounts and its useState is lost. Fix: either render both bodies with display:none toggling, OR lift text/mode/dirty into the parent component. Spec explicitly requires: 'edit Video textarea, switch to Chat, switch back to Video — text should persist in component state, not reset'.

initialScope prop is not respected when drawer is in Video mode. Opening the drawer, clicking ora-chat-mode-video-btn, then opening the rules panel still shows the Chat pill highlighted and hr-textarea (Chat body) rendered — video-house-rules-body is not mounted. Expected: panel should default to Video tab. Confirmed via computed background colours (chat pill = rgb(224,122,95), video pill = transparent). Likely mode toggle in drawer doesn't reach OraChatHouseRulesPanel, or the useState(initialScope) initialiser runs before the prop stabilises. Recommend verifying `mode` prop value at the drawer render site.

Cosmetic double-ellipsis in collapsed-state fal.ai fingerprint: displays 'BYOK (……9876)' because the JSX template already prefixes '…' while `key_hint` from backend also begins with '…'. Compare Deepgram row which correctly shows 'configured (……2345)' — same double-ellipsis bug actually exists there too. Fix: either drop the '…' in the JSX template (`BYOK (${data.fal_key_hint})`) or return a plain 4-char hint from `key_hint()`.

verified_working: Backend GET /api/aurem-dev/admin/video/secrets — 401 without auth, 200 with admin token
Backend PUT /api/aurem-dev/admin/video/secrets with fal_api_key='fal_test_key_12345' — returns fal_configured=true and fal_key_hint containing last-4
Backend DELETE /api/aurem-dev/admin/video/secrets/fal-key — 401 without auth, 200 with admin token, GET afterwards shows fal_configured=false and empty hint
Admin Settings 'Video generation keys' card collapsed summary shows 'Universal Key fallback' when no BYOK key
Admin Settings card expand ('Rotate / add keys') shows BOTH Deepgram AND new fal.ai input fields
Saving fal key via UI updates the collapsed summary to 'BYOK (……XXXX)', persists across page reload, and the 'remove' link reverts to Universal Key fallback (also fires success toast)
House Rules panel opens from ORA Chat drawer gear icon; hr-scope-switcher visible with hr-scope-chat + hr-scope-video pills
Chat tab (default): hr-textarea, hr-counter, hr-save, hr-reset, hr-version-{n} + hr-restore all render — no regression
Video tab: video-house-rules-body renders with pre-seeded rules_text='Never say the word guaranteed or promise specific revenue numbers.' and enforcement_mode='block' loaded from backend
Chat tab textarea does NOT leak the Video tab's test input (Chat state remains isolated)
action_items: Lift text/mode/dirty state up into OraChatHouseRulesPanel or render both bodies simultaneously (with visibility toggle) so switching tabs preserves per-scope edits — required by spec.
Fix initialScope handling so opening the House Rules panel from a drawer in Video mode defaults the switcher to the Video pill.

Remove the double-ellipsis in VideoPipelineKeysCard's collapsed summary (both fal.ai and Deepgram lines) — decide whether to strip '…' from the JSX template or from services/llm_config_store.key_hint().
critical_code_review_comments: OraChatHouseRulesPanel.jsx line 90: `scope === 'chat' ? <ChatRulesBody /> : <VideoRulesBody />` unmounts inactive body. This directly causes the two switcher bugs.

AdminSettingsPage.jsx line 1152 and 1156: prefixing '…' before `data.*_key_hint` produces double ellipsis because backend's key_hint helper already prefixes '…' (see services/llm_config_store.key_hint).

success_rate.frontend: 8/11 checks (state preservation + initialScope + cosmetic-ellipsis failed; all core happy paths + backend contract via UI pass)

seed_data_creation: None persistent — test cleans up its fake fal key via DELETE at end of both backend pytest and Playwright run. Preview DB now has fal_configured=false again.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend contract for /admin/video/secrets (Deepgram + fal.ai BYOK) is solid — reuse /app/backend/tests/test_fal_byok_secrets.py as regression. Frontend fal.ai UI wiring is solid EXCEPT the '……XXXX' double-ellipsis cosmetic issue (same on Deepgram row). For House Rules, after the fix, re-verify: (a) editing Video textarea, switching to Chat, back to Video preserves both text AND dirty state (Save button stays enabled); (b) opening panel from drawer in Video mode selects Video pill by default. Also confirm the Video body still loads seed rules_text from backend on first mount.
rca of the issue: State-loss bug: OraChatHouseRulesPanel uses conditional rendering (`scope === 'chat' ? <ChatRulesBody/> : <VideoRulesBody/>`), which unmounts the inactive body and destroys its local useState. Every re-mount re-fetches from the backend, so unsaved edits are lost. initialScope bug: even though `<OraChatHouseRulesPanel initialScope={mode} />` is passed correctly, the visible outcome on-screen is that opening the panel while drawer mode-video is active still lands on the Chat pill — either the drawer's `mode` state isn't yet 'video' at the moment the panel opens, or the prop value isn't what we expect. Both bugs sit inside `OraChatHouseRulesPanel.jsx` and its callsite in `OraChatDrawer.jsx` line 740.
